newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Rubin says rumor he leaving untrue.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Rubin says rumor he leaving untrue.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Wednesday rumors that surfaced last month that he would leave his post before year-end were "not true".
The New York Post reported in June rumors that Rubin planned to leave "well before" the end of the year.
"We're planning trips to Vienna in June of '98," Rubin told Reuters.
Rubin made the comment as he left a meeting with House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican.
Later, after financial markets closed, Treasury Department spokesman Howard Schloss told reporters at Treasury that Rubin has no plans to leave his post.
"He's not leaving," Schloss said, "In fact, yesterday he was making plans for travel next spring."
